requirements.quote:
The first Initial packet from a client contains the start or all of
   its first cryptographic handshake message, which for TLS is the
   ClientHello.
requirements.condition: For the first Initial packet sent by a client using TLS.
requirements.required_behavior: Include at least the beginning, and possibly all, of the client's first ClientHello message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send the first Initial packet without any portion of the first ClientHello.
requirements.why_checkable: The first client Initial can be decrypted and its CRYPTO data inspected for the beginning of the first ClientHello.

requirements.quote:
To
   avoid this, servers MAY use the Retry feature (see Section 8.1 of
   [QUIC-TRANSPORT]) to only buffer partial ClientHello messages from
   clients with a validated address.
requirements.condition: When a server wants to avoid buffering a partial ClientHello for a client whose address is not validated.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the server to use Retry and restrict partial-ClientHello buffering to clients with validated addresses.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reject an implementation solely because it sends Retry instead of buffering a partial ClientHello from an unvalidated address.
requirements.why_checkable: A fragmented ClientHello from an unvalidated address can be used to observe whether the allowed Retry-and-defer-buffering policy is applied.

requirements.quote:
QUIC packet and framing add at least 36 bytes of overhead to the
   ClientHello message.
requirements.condition: When placing a ClientHello in a QUIC packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Account for at least 36 bytes beyond the ClientHello message itself for QUIC packet and framing overhead.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not calculate the resulting QUIC packet as adding fewer than 36 bytes of packet-and-framing overhead.
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized packet size minus the carried ClientHello bytes can be measured and compared with the stated lower bound.

requirements.quote:
That overhead increases if the client chooses a
   Source Connection ID field longer than zero bytes.
requirements.condition: If a client chooses a non-empty Source Connection ID for a packet carrying ClientHello.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the additional Source Connection ID contribution in the packet overhead.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not treat overhead with a non-empty Source Connection ID as equal to the zero-length Source Connection ID baseline.
requirements.why_checkable: Otherwise equivalent serialized packets with empty and non-empty Source Connection IDs can be compared to verify the increase.

requirements.quote:
The TLS implementation does not need to ensure that the ClientHello
   is large enough to meet QUIC's requirements for datagrams that carry
   Initial packets; see Section 14.1 of [QUIC-TRANSPORT].
requirements.condition: When constructing a ClientHello for carriage in a datagram containing an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the TLS implementation to produce the ClientHello without padding it to satisfy QUIC's datagram-size requirement.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not require the TLS implementation itself to make the ClientHello large enough for QUIC's Initial-datagram sizing rule.
requirements.why_checkable: An integration test can use a small TLS-produced ClientHello and verify that conformance does not depend on TLS padding it to the QUIC datagram size.

requirements.quote:
QUIC
   implementations use PADDING frames or packet coalescing to ensure
   that datagrams are large enough.
requirements.condition: When a datagram carrying an Initial packet would otherwise be smaller than QUIC requires.
requirements.required_behavior: Use PADDING frames or packet coalescing to make the datagram large enough.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send an undersized datagram carrying an Initial packet.
requirements.why_checkable: The responsibility and allowed mechanisms are clear, but this chunk does not provide the minimum datagram size needed to turn 'large enough' into a self-contained concrete check.
